Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. HealthSync legal and privacy are spinning up our onboarding checklist and have a couple of narrow asks before we sign the DPA annex: primarily around PII egress paths from your hosted runtime and proof that exported artifacts (logs, telemetry) are pseudonymized or encrypted at rest. Specifically: 

- A diagram showing all egress destinations for request/telemetry/alerts (including third-party analytics and cloud vendor endpoints).
- Confirmation whether any PII leaves your VPC to third-party subprocessors and which subprocessors (name + location).

We need these items to feed into our security questionnaire. Can you send artifacts or point to a shared location? Procurement is copied and will want to lock a narrow SLA on retention after onboarding completes.

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and we’ll follow with artifacts: 

- Egress diagram: we have an updated diagram (attached) that maps runtime egress: telemetry -> Datadog (US), alerts -> PagerDuty (US), optional analytics -> Segment (US/EU) when customers opt in. No PII is intentionally forwarded to analytics.
- Subprocessors: short list included in the DPA annex; primary ones for exports are our cloud vendor (AWS us-west-2) and Datadog (logs ingest). We’ll include locations and SCC/legal basis in the annex draft.
- KMS custody: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS for Private deployments and a managed KMS option for Hosted. For hosted customers who require BYOK for logs, we offer a dedicated key proxy; details and attestation are attached.

I’m attaching three files: redwood-dpa-annex-v1.pdf, egress-diagram-v2.png, kms-attestation-2026.txt. Marissa, Mina — can you please review the diagram and the attestation and add any technical caveats (key rotation window, telemetry retention defaults) before EOD Monday?

On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 10:03 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’m attaching three files: redwood-dpa-annex-v1.pdf, egress-diagram-v2.png, kms-attestation-2026.txt. Marissa, Mina — can you please review the diagram and the attestation and add any technical caveats (key rotation window, telemetry retention defaults) before EOD Monday?

Thanks Ben. A few clarifications for HealthSync to avoid follow-ups: 

- PII flow: runtime request payloads are processed on ephemeral containers. We persist only token-level telemetry; request payloads are not stored unless the customer explicitly enables logging for debugging. When logging is enabled, logs are pseudonymized by default (PHI/PII redaction rules applied) and stored encrypted with AES-256.
- Exports: exported artifacts for onboarding (e.g., traces, SRE logs) go to Object Storage in the customer tenant (for Dedicated/Private) or to our managed bucket for Hosted customers. Hosted exported logs to Datadog contain metadata and sampling IDs only; raw PII is redacted/pseudonymized before export.
- KMS: for Hosted customers we manage the root KMS key but can create a dedicated data-encryption key per customer. BYOK is available for Private and Dedicated via our KMS proxy. Key rotation: 90 days default; customers can request alignment to their rotation policy on contract.

Daniel — I’ll call out these points in the DPA annex draft (section 3.2–3.4) and include a short exportability checklist as an appendix. If HealthSync requires a stronger attestation (e.g., HSM-backed key custody), we can scope that into a support addendum.

Marissa
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben and Marissa — that’s helpful and addresses most of our checklist. A couple of follow-ups before procurement will sign: 

- Can you enumerate the subprocessors by role (e.g., metrics ingestion, monitoring, alerting) and attach an exported roster with city/country? We need to confirm there are no EU-only PII transfers outside EU without SCCs.

If you can drop the roster and a one-page sample log and retention options into the shared drive this afternoon we’ll loop legal and procurement and aim to finish the DPA annex sign-off by EOD Thursday.
